groups.title: The Commands window — how it runs what you paste
groups.desc: Common Functionality User Guide 2.1, Command Window. The window opens from Home → Windows and is hidden by default. The key fact: a plain paste runs every line as a separate command, so a multi-line block never comes together. The right-click menu has a second item that solves it.

groups.title: Where to stand — navigation
groups.desc: Almost every command works on the current element (CE). First stand on it, then act.

groups.title: Create — cable trays
groups.desc: The order is exactly this: tray, branch, section, head and tail, route, point coordinates.

groups.title: Create — equipment

groups.title: Find and look
groups.desc: Read-only. These commands change nothing — use them freely.

groups.title: Change
groups.desc: These write to the database. There is no UNDO command, but rollback exists and is verified: MARKDB |label| before the operation, UNDODB back to it, UNDODB n — n marks back. Its one limit is verified too: SAVEWORK erases the mark, after saving UNDODB answers «No mark to UNDO to». Order of work: mark, change, check, and only then SAVEWORK.

groups.title: Show on screen

groups.title: Drawings and isometrics (DRAW module)
groups.desc: IsoADP is NOT in this build: the DRAW module has no Isometric Automatic Drawing Production item and ISOADP $Q gives CP: Syntax error. The 2.1 docs describe it, but the licence is different. An isometric is therefore an ordinary view with an isometric direction, built with the commands below. NEW DRWG $Q and ISODRAFT $Q print their syntax, so the commands exist; they were not run.

groups.title: Beyond E3D — files and Windows
groups.desc: Found in real PML code, then verified by runs. Works from a macro file (Paste as Macro) and needs neither admin rights nor PMLLIB. Cyrillic and other non-Latin text passes on write but NOT on read — see the ReadFile row.

groups.title: Variables and substitution
groups.desc: Works right in the Command Line. Anything beyond substitution lives in a macro file — see the next section.

groups.title: The PML language — works in a macro file, not in the Command Line
groups.desc: E3D 2.1 runs PML2 with full backward compatibility with PML1: one interpreter, both syntaxes work and mix in real macros. Anything longer than one line will not run from a plain paste — each line goes as a separate command (if and endif each fail on their own). The way out is in the docs: right-click → Paste as Macro writes the paste to a temporary file and runs it as a macro, and there blocks work. So logic can run straight from the Commands window — just from a different menu item.

rows.note: Word for word: «executes each line of the copied text as a separate command as if they had been typed». That is why an if line fails with «Invalid syntax» — it runs alone. And on the first error the remaining lines of the paste do NOT run — the tail has to be entered again.
Word for word: «first creates a temporary file containing the copied macro commands and executes this as a macro». This is how if, do and handle work — and it is faster for many commands.
«Macro files can also be dragged into the command window».
Arguments $1…$9 work.
